authors_reviews.title: This brush is a great doggy massage tool.
authors_reviews.text: I’m a professional dog groomer. I don’t typically use a brush when I’m lathering up a dog in the tub. However, I liked the idea of this brush for that reason the handle of it being directly above allows you to gently brush down the dogs back to spread the shampoo a lot better.As soon as I got the brush, I liked the way it felt in my hand. It’s a good size. Lightweight it’s not something that you’re going to use to brush out knots on a dog. This is more for a shorter haired dog that you are trying to distribute the shampoo or give the dog a massage.I immediately used it on both of my golden retrievers backs (not in the tub) and I’ll be honest their reactions were quite positive. They both leaned into it and really liked having it on their backs. The teeth of the brush our wide and flexible so I imagine it feels really good down the back of these length coats. Again, if the dog has long hair, this is not something that I would toy with because you don’t wanna tangle the hair but if you have a dog with shorter hair like a golden retriever or a lab or a German Shepherd, I think this brush would be great. But again, this is not something that you’re using to shed an animal even though yes it does remove some of the fur as you’re brushing them, but I would treat it more as a positive tool. Think of it as a massage tool for your dog that is a bonus because it does remove some hair during the process of massaging them. To remove the hair, you press the button and it pushes the loose hair forward for you to collect. Nice and easy. I have not used it in the tub yet, but I know 100%. It will do the job for now. I hold the brush up and I ask them if they want a massage and they both get super excited. Both dogs lean into it and want their back done. I even let the kids take turns because it’s that easy to use. And of course with everything I always suggest being gentle. Brushing too hard, no matter what the breed or brush will scrape and damage the skin. Gentle, slow and steady is key.
authors_reviews.author: Melissa

authors_reviews.title: A handy self-cleaning brush that makes bathing pets and clearing loose fur super fast and easy!
authors_reviews.text: As someone who has never used a self-cleaning pet scrubber before, I was really impressed by how practical this tool feels right out of the box. The brush features a rounded hand-grip top that fits comfortably in your palm, giving you total control while brushing down your pet during baths or dry coat maintenance. The tall plastic bristles are firm yet flexible enough to work through dense fur, gathering loose undercoat and dander into a neat pad that pops right off when you press the top push button.Priced at $13 at the time of this review, it is an affordable option that stays right in line with similar multi-use pet bath brushes on the market. Like other reviewers, I also found that the one-click hair release mechanism makes cleaning out trapped fur infinitely faster and far less messy than manually digging hair out of traditional wire or rubber comb teeth. Overall, whether you are trying to lather up shampoo in the tub or keep everyday shedding under control, this little pink scrubber makes grooming feel like a breeze.ProsConvenient one-click push button ejects trapped fur instantly.Comfortable ergonomic palm grip gives great leverage while brushing.Versatile design works for both wet bath scrubbing and dry coat detangling.Gentle bristles help lather up shampoo while lifting out loose hair.ConsPlastic bristles might feel a bit firm for pets with extremely sensitive skin.Compact size means grooming larger dog breeds will take a few extra passes.
authors_reviews.author: Vincent Wu

authors_reviews.title: Ok for dogs, great for husbands?
authors_reviews.text: I bought this to use for bath time with my Goldendoodle. I had a different scrub brush, but the nubbins/bristles were so large that it didn't seem to work all that well.This one does work a bit better because the bristles can really get into her super thick, dense coat, but because her skin is so loose, it still just kind of moves things around a lot and doesn't seem super comfortable. It was, however, more comfortable for me to use on her because the handle is designed really well. I used it once, and then cleaned it up, which was super easy with the little hair removing mechanism, and put it on the bathroom counter, unsure of what to do with it.Well, my dear husband, who has been known to use the leftover foaming dog shampoo when I make too big of a batch for a single bath, decided that since he was already using dog shampoo as body wash, he would give this scrubbing brush a try too. Keep in mind, he's not a super hairy guy - some hair, yes, but not sasquatch-like or unreasonably hairy.Let me tell you... the way this man RAVED about how nice this brush felt on his skin. I couldn't help but laugh. Whatever it takes to give him a satisfying shower experience, I guess.So, yes, this works totally fine for dogs, but as a bonus, it also works great on semi-hairy husbands.
authors_reviews.author: D.

The brush works well for both wet and dry grooming, making it useful between baths too. 🧼🐕The purple color is cute, and the handle feels comfortable to hold while brushing. authors_reviews.title: My cat liked it, as I massaged his back with it. Will work well for intended purpose!
authors_reviews.text: My cat liked it, as I massaged his back with it. Will work well for intended purpose!This brush was easy to hold and my cat seemed to enjoy being brushed/massaged with it. I did find that I had to use a light touch because he didn’t like it when I pressed too hard. Overall, it’s an easy-to-use grooming brush that worked well with a gentle hand.The brush is simple and easy to use. The bristles are pointy, but would be soft enough to be gentle while still helping work shampoo through a pet’s coat.It’s comfortable to hold and easy to rinse clean afterward. (There really was no collection of hair in the brush after I brushed my cat. I think that is because the bristles are so far apart.) It kinda works more like a massage brush & if they enjoy it, as a great bonding tool to bond with your cat or dog.. 🙂 but will work well for it's intended purpose; to work shampoo through the pet's coat during bath time. I think this brush would work really well on a long haired dog.A handy grooming tool, for everyday use to brush the pets coat, massage their backs & to use for bath time.

authors_reviews.text: This is a handheld dog bath scrubber with built-in deshedding action.This is a completely submersible all plastic dog brush for bath time that cleans itself. authors_reviews.title: Makes Bath Time and Shedding Much Easier!!!!! 🫧
authors_reviews.text: This dog bath brush has been a really handy addition to our grooming routine. The bristles are soft enough to be comfortable for my pet while still doing a good job of loosening and removing loose fur. I especially like that it can be used both wet and dry, so I can use it during bath time or for regular brushing.The one-click hair release is probably my favorite feature. Instead of having to pull all the collected fur out of the brush by hand, it releases the hair quickly and makes cleanup much easier. It also fits comfortably in my hand and is easy to maneuver while bathing or brushing.The purple color is cute, and the brush feels sturdy without being too bulky. Overall, it’s a convenient grooming tool that helps with shedding and makes bath time a little less messy and much more manageable.

authors_reviews.title: MY DOGS THINK THIS SCRUBBER IS AMAZING
authors_reviews.text: If you have pets, you'll be interested in this OLAEMUO DOG BATH BRUSH. It's a multitude of good things! As a dog brush it will help control your pets shedding. I say pet because it's good for both dogs and cats. After brushing your pet, when you depress the center of the handle (plunger) it moves a solid plastic plate down the bristles pushing the pet hair out so you can remove it easily from the scrubber. You can bath your dogs with it and use it to lather up the shampoo. It works as a terrific massager for your pet too. PLUS! If you don't want to use it for your pets, it's a great scalp massager for you! I tested it and it's wonderful as a scalp massager. The bristles are not hard plastic; they are pliable and bend. They are stiff enough to lather or massage but they bend with the shape of what they're massaging. I may have to order another one so that I can dedicate one to myself for scalp massaging while I watch TV....it's THAT good!
